subject: Social Habits
title: My feelings
objectives: Children will name happy, sad, angry and scared.
Children will show feelings with their faces and bodies.
content: Naming happy and sad, angry and scared, and showing feelings with faces and bodies.
teachingActivities: Use real faces, mirrors and picture cards; name feelings as they happen ("You look sad"); never say a feeling is wrong; keep feelings words simple; model calm responses; use a feelings chart every day.
learnerActivities: Name happy, sad, angry and scared and show them with the face and body.
resources: Pictures of children with different feelings
assessment: Observe whether each child names two or more feelings and shows a feeling with their face.
expectedOutcomes: Shows a feeling with the face.

lessons.title: Happy and sad
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will name happy and sad and show them with their faces.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have practised greetings, please and thank you.
resources: Feelings face cards: happy and sad
lessons.starter: Show a happy face and a sad face and say "I feel happy. I feel sad. Everyone has feelings."
teacherActivities: Show the happy face and smile together.
Show the sad face and make a sad face.
Let children look in the mirror and show each feeling.
learnerActivities: Children smile and say happy.
Children make a sad face and say sad.
Child shows happy and sad in the mirror.
Child says or points to something.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the happy face and smile together. Children: Children smile and say happy.
Step 2. Teacher: Show the sad face and make a sad face. Children: Children make a sad face and say sad.
Step 3. Teacher: Let children look in the mirror and show each feeling. Children: Child shows happy and sad in the mirror.
Step 4. Teacher: Ask "What makes you happy?" Children: Child says or points to something.

practical.title: Mirror faces
practical.safety: Use a safe unbreakable mirror and supervise closely. Never say that sad is bad; say that all feelings are okay.

differentiation.support: Show the face and name the feeling together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say why a friend might be sad.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How do you feel when you play?
How does a sad face look?

expectedOutcomes: Shows happy and sad with the face
lessons.homeConnection: Name feelings at home: "You look happy" or "You look sad."
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name happy and sad and show them with their faces" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

learnerFacing.songOrRhyme: If you are happy and you know it, clap your hands.

lessons.title: Angry and scared
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will name angry and scared and show them with their faces.
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have practised greetings, please and thank you.
resources: Feelings face cards: angry and scared
lessons.starter: Show an angry face and a scared face and say "Sometimes we feel cross or scared. That is okay."
teacherActivities: Show the angry face and make a cross face.
Show the scared face and make a scared face.
Use the puppet to show what scared feels like and give it a hug.
Say "A grown-up can help us when we feel big feelings."
learnerActivities: Children make an angry face and say angry.
Children make a scared face and say scared.
Children say it is okay.
Child points to a trusted adult.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the angry face and make a cross face. Children: Children make an angry face and say angry.
Step 2. Teacher: Show the scared face and make a scared face. Children: Children make a scared face and say scared.
Step 3. Teacher: Use the puppet to show what scared feels like and give it a hug. Children: Children say it is okay.
Step 4. Teacher: Say "A grown-up can help us when we feel big feelings." Children: Child points to a trusted adult.

practical.title: Feelings faces
steps: Make each face in the mirror.
practical.safety: Keep the activity gentle and calm so it does not frighten children. Stop if a child is upset and comfort them.

differentiation.support: Show the face and name the feeling together.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say what helps when they are scared.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: How do you look when you are angry?

lessons.conclusion: Take a deep breath and smile.
lessons.homeConnection: Name big feelings at home and say "I can help you."
teacherReflection: Which children could show "name angry and scared and show them with their faces" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Feelings faces
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will match faces to feeling words and show feelings with their bodies.
successCriteria: Matches a face to a feeling word
Shows a feeling with the body
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have practised greetings, please and thank you.
lessons.starter: Show a feelings card and say "How does this child feel?"
teacherActivities: Hold up a feelings card and name it.
Say "Show me happy" and let children show it.
Play "Show me" for sad, angry and scared.
Let each child choose a card and show the feeling.
learnerActivities: Children say the feeling.
Child shows happy with face and body.
Child shows each feeling.
Friends guess the feeling.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Hold up a feelings card and name it. Children: Children say the feeling.
Step 2. Teacher: Say "Show me happy" and let children show it. Children: Child shows happy with face and body.
Step 3. Teacher: Play "Show me" for sad, angry and scared. Children: Child shows each feeling.
Step 4. Teacher: Let each child choose a card and show the feeling. Children: Friends guess the feeling.

practical.title: Show me a feeling
practical.safety: Keep the floor clear and supervise movement. Stop the game if a child becomes upset.

differentiation.support: Offer two cards and name the feeling.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to show a feeling and say why.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

teacherReflection: Which children could show "match faces to feeling words and show feelings with their bodies" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: How do I feel today?
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Children will choose a face on the feelings chart to show how they feel.
successCriteria: Says a feeling word with support
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have practised greetings, please and thank you.
resources: A feelings chart with four faces
lessons.starter: Show the feelings chart and say "Every morning we show how we feel."
teacherActivities: Show the four faces on the chart.
Call each child to put their name tag on a face.
Say "Thank you for telling me" and listen.
Talk about how to help someone who is sad.
learnerActivities: Children look and name them.
Child chooses a face and places the tag.
Child says a word or points.
Children give a hug or a smile if they wish.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Show the four faces on the chart. Children: Children look and name them.
Step 2. Teacher: Call each child to put their name tag on a face. Children: Child chooses a face and places the tag.
Step 3. Teacher: Say "Thank you for telling me" and listen. Children: Child says a word or points.
Step 4. Teacher: Talk about how to help someone who is sad. Children: Children give a hug or a smile if they wish.

practical.title: Feelings chart
steps: Put your name on a face.
practical.safety: Never judge a feeling. Offer comfort and let children choose whether to be touched. Offer a wave or a high five instead of a hug.

differentiation.support: Offer two faces and help the child choose.
differentiation.extension: Ask the child to say why they chose that face.

assessment.method: Observe each child during the practical activity and note Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding on the class record. Ask the questions below one to one or in a small group.

questions.question: Why do you feel that?
questions.expected: Child gives a reason or points.

expectedOutcomes: Says how they feel with support
lessons.homeConnection: Ask your child how they feel each day.
teacherReflection: Which children could show "choose a face on the feelings chart to show how they feel" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?

lessons.title: Week 4 feelings check
lessons.subject: Social Habits
objectives: Teachers will observe how each child names and shows feelings.
successCriteria: Shows a feeling with the face
lessons.previousKnowledge: Children have practised greetings, please and thank you.
lessons.starter: Sing the feelings song and show three stations.
teacherActivities: Set up three stations: faces, chart and story.
At each station ask "How does this feel?" and watch.
learnerActivities: Children rotate every four minutes.
Child answers with a word or face.
Children tidy at the signal.
presentation: Step 1. Teacher: Set up three stations: faces, chart and story. Children: Children rotate every four minutes.
Step 2. Teacher: At each station ask "How does this feel?" and watch. Children: Child answers with a word or face.
Step 3. Teacher: Record each child’s level. Children: Children tidy at the signal.

practical.title: Feelings stations
practical.safety: Supervise each station and keep the floor clear. Stop any activity that distresses a child.

differentiation.support: Provide an adult partner and use two feelings.
differentiation.extension: Ask a confident child to teach a friend.

assessment.method: Observe and record Emerging, Developing, Secure or Exceeding for: names happy and sad; names angry and scared; shows feelings with the face; points to a helper.

expectedOutcomes: Has an observation record for Week 4
teacherReflection: Which children could show "Teachers will observe how each child names and shows feelings" without help, and who needs another turn tomorrow?
What did the children say or do that I did not expect, and how will I use it in the next lesson?
Which resource or instruction worked best, and what would I change before I teach this again?
